The bullet states that at the shipped bytes a grep count of run_t007_ definitions reports seventeen, and declares that sentence to be the ONLY live statement of that count. Counting the definitions in this bundle's own copy of the shared block-suite driver gives eighteen, and all eighteen are wired into the driver's run list, so nothing is dead. The report's own Files Changed bullet twenty lines earlier says eighteen, which both contradicts the seventeen and falsifies the only-live-statement claim. Round 28 added the post-block-journal case and the count was not re-measured. This is a recurrence of the finding the report records as round 25's Major (the same sentence then read sixteen against a true seventeen), and the count verifier written in response to that round did not catch the recurrence. The number understates coverage, so this is staleness rather than fabrication, but the report itself draws the distinction that a stale value framed as a MEASUREMENT is the more serious form.

The narrative says mutant R dies at 391/1. The mutation capture records MUTANT R at RESULT: 394 passed, 1 failed against a 395/0 clean control. The mutation log itself is internally sound - I counted nineteen mutants A through S, a clean control at 395/0 at the top, F, O and Q sitting at the control tally and labelled UNCOVERED with their arguments stated, and every other mutant strictly below the control - so only the prose figure is wrong.

The comment describes the panel-round-6 RED captures as the red that matches the shipped, post-remediation code. Measured, those captures carry 345 assertions (341 passing, 4 failing) while the shipped suite carries 395, so they cannot be the red of the shipped driver; they are the red of the round-6 driver, and their four failures are confined to one fixture. The task's own acceptance-first RED does exist in the bundle at 272 passing / 23 failing in both runtimes and is not what red_evidence points at. The substitute non-vacuity evidence for rounds 7 to 28 is the mutation log, which is present and adequate, so this is a characterisation defect rather than missing evidence.

The frozen task entry carries Cross-Model: not enabled while the verification contract sets cross_model to required. The contract states a coherent reason (Security-Sensitive: true makes the ship step treat cross-model as a hard pre-gate) and the check is correctly left DEFAULT-FAIL at passes:false, so the two are reconcilable, but the frozen record and the contract literally disagree on the same field.
